impact:
Found during pre-publish verification of the packaged tarball.

Two user-facing messages in the published package tell people to run a command that is not reachable from a global install:

1. setup.ts prints "✓ Zug: created PERSONA.md — run 'zug onboard' to seed your cognitive fingerprint". The CLI's command dispatch has no `onboard` case. Its full command set is: --version, archive, backup, compact, persona, pull, push, resume, setup, status, sync, tail, update, version.

2. cli.ts prints "No PERSONA.md found. Run 'pnpm onboard' to create one." — a repo-local pnpm script surfacing in a globally installed binary, where there is no repo and no pnpm workspace.

So a new user completing `zug setup` is told to run a command that exits with an unknown-command path, on the very first thing they are asked to do after install. This is the first-run experience for the OSS package and, later, for paying users.

CONTRIBUTING FACT: dist/onboard.js exists in the build but is deliberately NOT in package.json's `files` allowlist, and nothing in the published require graph reaches it — so the onboarding flow those messages point at is not shipped at all.

FIX DIRECTION: decide whether onboarding is part of the published product. If yes, add an `onboard` command to the CLI dispatch and add dist/onboard.js to `files`. If no, rewrite both messages to name something that exists (or fold the seeding step into `zug setup`). Either way the two messages should agree with each other and with the shipped command set.

Related: the sibling packaging defect where dist/version-check.js was required by cli.js but omitted from `files` (fixed in e3983ec) — both come from the `files` allowlist being maintained by hand with nothing checking it against the actual require graph. A test that resolves the published entrypoints' imports against the allowlist would catch this whole class.
title: Published CLI points users at a `zug onboard` command that does not exist
